primary_question: Can a query-blind, resource-bounded native learned-associative and learned-composition mechanism answer causal-sign queries across unfamiliar entity identities and changed graph structures better than equally informed trained recurrent and exact symbolic controls?
candidate_mechanism: fixed 8-record query-blind key-value fast memory; trained 16-bit key feature reliability and 4-hidden-neuron neural composition; trainable associative retrieval without entity-indexed slots

task.entities: unique 8-bit IDs, with independent query and observation nuisance features
task.edges: directed signed causal links, shuffled in an 8-record store without fixed entity-to-slot mapping
task.training_graphs: two- and three-hop linear DAGs with disconnected distractors
task.development_graphs: three-hop unseen entity assignments and structure permutations
task.stress_graphs: four-hop chains with disconnected cycle/distractor, novel entity-ID block
task.query: source entity and requested causal horizon; no query during retention
task.label: signed intervention influence of complete path, from source-free graph generator only (never inserted as memory key or rule)
task.model: trainable 4-hidden-unit tanh composition network; no built-in sign-product composition during inference
task.key_encoder: trainable per-feature reliability for stable entity bits vs per-visit nuisance bits; no raw entity equality in candidate recall
task.physical_capacity: at most 8 retained causal edges, no unbounded task-specific memory

training.training_supervision: train-only prefix influence labels and contrastive same-vs-different entity pairs
training.candidate_test_info: same observations and horizon available to controls

controls: train-fitted recurrent tanh network with equal trainable compose parameters and identical edge information
exact symbolic graph traversal upper bound

acceptance.strict_decision: ACCEPT_DEVELOPMENT_SIGNAL_ONLY only if every requirement met; otherwise NEGATIVE, invalid source/design if fairness/leakage breaks
